simple.meaning: הֲמֻלָּה (hămullâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “a sound.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: הֲמֻלָּה (H1999) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Jeremiah 11:16, with occurrences in Jeremiah, Ezekiel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to הֲמֻלָּה (H1999) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in הֲמֻלָּה (H1999) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: הֲמֻלָּה (hămullâh) / H1999 is traced through Jeremiah 11:16, Ezekiel 1:24 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H1999. hamullah הֲמוּלָּה הֲמֻלָּה, noun feminine rain-storm (?), rushing or roaring sound (?): גְדֹלָה הֲמוּלָּה קוֺל Jer 11:16 sound of a great storm , of wind fanning flames in tree (in figurative of Yahweh's judgement on Judah); > AV RV Da tumult ; מַחֲנֶה כְּקוֺל הֲמֻלָּה קוֺל Ezek 1:24 of noise of wings of living creatures in Ezekiel's vision (strike out B Co compare Hi).
definitions.rootNote: or (too fully) הֲמוּלָּה ; (Jeremiah 11:16), feminine passive participle of an unused root meaning to rush (as rain with a windy roar);
